examples.description: Play live audio with a strong kick (a mix or a drum bus) plus a MIDI controller: CC 1-13 summon, hold and shape the god, pad 36 collapses it, pads 37-44 pick a god. The Live panel's Response controls shape what the conductor hears: Transients which kicks count (and collapse the god), Sensitivity and Sustain the spectrum the matter reads, Attack and Release its envelopes. The Live panel's Response controls set what it hears: Sensitivity how loud the music reads (a quiet input drives the arc less), Transients the snare and hat (on a mix the kick follows the beat clock while the drums play; a drum input keyed drums gives the real one). See docs/prototypes/digital-mosh/03-implementation.md.

examples.description: Play live audio by channel: up to four sources with the roles drums, bass, synth and vocal (or any other), one porcelain mannequin bust each -- one to four busts, as many as there are sources, laid out for the count; a plain mix gives one. Each bust speaks its own channel like a noise gate: on a note the neck snaps back, the lips part and rays of light shoot from the mouth; between notes they look round the room, eyes darting. Each source is a different corrupted transmission: the drums suffer tracking failure (torn bands, static, channels jumping), the bass codec collapse (displaced macroblocks that persist), the synth broadcast interference (static, scanlines, drifting colour channels), a vocal or other source temporal ghosting. MIDI: CC 1 master, CC 2 rays, CC 3 gate sensitivity, CC 4 effects, CC 5 tearing, CC 6 colour, CC 7 gain, CC 8 palette, CC 9 head tilt (each rests at its middle and picks up); pad 36 holds every gate shut, 37 holds them open, 39 bursts. Opening it turns live input on (View > Live); PageUp/PageDown step through the Sonic Abstract set. docs/prototypes/talking-heads/.

examples.description: Play Sabertooth: its stems each perform a part of the frame (or, live, input channels keyed the same way); optionally a MIDI controller, CC 21-28 for Cloud Diving, Crash, Moog, Kick, Snare, Toms, tone block and Bass (each part's contribution, resting at full). A flight down a winding mirror river through a valley of faceted indigo mountains at dusk, under an enormous sky of layered aurora ribbons. The Cloud Diving swells twist and recolour the aurora; each crash throws a fireball across the valley; each kick, snare and tom sends a pulse of light down its own lane of the river, lighting the riverbed and the fish under the water, with a splash behind the camera; the bass lights the left bank (from its MIDI file, BASS.mid beside the stems, when it is there) and the Moog the right, in bands running down the ranges. On a mix alone the aurora still follows the mix and the accents rest. The Feline Footwear version is the hidden entry 'Sonic VFX - Aurora Borealis (Feline Footwear)'. Run examples/aurora-borealis/build.py first (pure Python, about a minute). See docs/prototypes/aurora-borealis/.

Play live audio (any mix) and, optionally, a MIDI controller: CC 1 excitation, CC 2 complexity, CC 3 persistence, CC 4 spatial scale, CC 5 terrain, CC 8 light, CC 9 palette, CC 10 lock; pad 36 strike. A night basin whose ground is a resonating plate: the music excites one designed bank of standing waves, and its nodal lines stand as ridges between sunken antinodes, carving rings, petals and cells that wander and re-form with the music. Ten artist palettes take turns at phrase boundaries (or on a big change in the music when there is no tempo), blended in OKLab; CC 9 picks one, CC 10 holds it. The ground's figure is drawn by one resonance field (ADR-1400, ADR-1403 to 1409); the scene carries no track of its own. See docs/prototypes/cymatic-world/.

examples.description: Play live audio (any mix) and, optionally, a MIDI controller: CC 1 resonance, CC 2 fold depth, CC 3 wave travel, CC 4 surface detail, CC 5 iridescence, CC 6 light response, CC 7 color drift, CC 8 motion scale, CC 9 palette, CC 10 palette lock. One immense sheet of iridescent silk, gathered at invisible anchors and spreading broad between them, hangs in a dark void; the music excites it as a resonator: bass bows the sheet, mids crease it, highs run light along its folds, and onsets send wavefronts across it. See docs/prototypes/resonant-silk/02-report.md.

A kinetic wall of nearly ten thousand metal flaps, each turned by its own oscillator: when they fall into step the whole wall turns and flashes as one; as the coupling loosens it breaks into islands that turn against each other, and travelling waves sweep bands of light across it. An R&D experiment: see docs/prototypes/generative-rd/A-oscillators.md.

A vast mineral plain whose surface is grown, not carved: a reaction-diffusion pattern raises ridges and cells out of the stone, and the frontier between two pattern families wanders across it, rewriting the relief as it passes. An R&D experiment: see docs/prototypes/generative-rd/C-reaction-diffusion.md.

examples.description: Play live audio (any mix) and, optionally, a MIDI controller: CC 1 pattern, CC 2 seeding, CC 3 pin height, CC 4 audio influence, CC 5 erase, CC 6 light, CC 7 waves, CC 8 impact, CC 9 palette, CC 10 palette lock, CC 11 shimmer, notes 36-38 hold seeds. A living, illuminated topographic interference field: a bowl of pins in the dark, a reaction-diffusion labyrinth growing over it, its edges drawn as contours of light (a fine hot core, a softer halo, dark channels between). A broad swell heaves the field, crossing the bass history's rings; it bunches and opens the contours and runs beads of light along them on the hats; the bass history rolls out from the heart as a lift and a pool of light; every kick sends a ring of impact across it that swells the contours, carries a band of light and turns the labyrinth toward spots; a busy mix lights it up, a breakdown lets it settle. See docs/prototypes/generative-rd/C-scene-plan.md and docs/prototypes/generative-pass/.

examples.description: Play live audio (any mix) and, optionally, a MIDI controller: CC 1 coupling, CC 2 complexity, CC 3 motion, CC 4 audio influence, CC 5 lag, CC 6 light, CC 7 swell, CC 8 impact, CC 9 palette, CC 10 palette lock, CC 11 shimmer, note 36 holds a pacemaker. An immense membrane of luminous vertical blades round the inside of a sphere: about eighteen thousand blades, each swung by its own oscillator, falling into step and breaking apart round the viewer, the music travelling through the surface as rings, swells and streaks of light. The bass history rolls out across the membrane as rings, the held sound swells it and pulls the blades toward unison, kicks push a ring through it and launch a phase front round the sphere, the snare a quicker one, hats run streaks up the blades; six palettes take turns at phrase boundaries (or on a big change in the music when there is no tempo). See docs/prototypes/phase-wall/ and docs/prototypes/generative-pass/.
examples.name: Phase Hall

examples.description: Play live audio (any mix) and, optionally, a MIDI controller: CC 1 rainbow glow, CC 2 lens (fisheye to rectilinear), CC 5 haze, CC 6 light, CC 7 colour, CC 9 look (Bright Noon, Golden Hour, After the Storm, Lavender Dusk, Prism, Candy, Electric, Spring), CC 10 look lock (unlocked, the look moves on at phrase boundaries or a big change in the music). The Rainbow Knot: a painterly meadow world knotted through an all-round sky. A fisheye ride flies low and fast over hills, flower fields and groves on a 5.7 km twisting band of land; gravity turns with the land, the ride swings over the rims onto the band's other face, and it slows under rainbow arches above a sea of clouds. The world plays the music, mostly in colour and light: the synth lights the rainbows (bands of light flowing along them), the clouds, the sky and a shimmer across the flower fields; the bass deepens the meadow's colour; each kick pops the grass round you, the hats glint in it and the claps brighten the arches; and at the drop a world scan races out and turns the land, the stones and the trees to rainbow for a few seconds. The ride glides fast and low over the land and swings round its rims. It follows drum, bass and synth stems when a multichannel input maps channels to them (Live panel, Inputs), and the main mix otherwise. Rainbow World (offline), under Offline > Worlds, is the same world at full quality for renders. Run examples/rainbow-world/build.py first (Blender 5.x; it writes the scene). See docs/prototypes/rainbow-world/.

examples.description: Rainbow World at full quality, for renders: the Rainbow Knot's painterly meadow world knotted through an all-round sky, a fisheye ride low and fast over its hills, flower fields and groves, round its rims and under rainbow arches. It plays whatever it is given -- the Feline Footwear mix here -- with the live version's reactivity: the synth lights the rainbows, clouds and sky, the bass deepens the colour and makes the clouds breathe, the drums pop the grass and brighten the arches, and on a big synth swell a world scan turns the land to rainbow while the trees twirl and burst like fireworks. A project can name drum, bass and synth stems to follow them. Song-agnostic: no timing is baked for any track; a song's own video bakes its scans, camera and looks over this one (a `distort` macro warps the world, for an ending). Run examples/rainbow-world/build.py first (Blender 5.x; it writes both scenes). See docs/prototypes/rainbow-world/.
